files.note: Read the whole file: offerable/locked/left_in_place, scan_project, the scan_once leader flight, cleanup_remove, cleanup_sizes and the preselection tests. Selection is gated on Kolux's own record and never forces, and sizes are read on demand; no provable defect found.

Read the whole file: folder_ids/unflag_write/add_folder, project_add_folder, project_remove, end_sessions and the F1/F79/R02 tests. Removal ends each folder's sessions once and spares a staying nested project; no provable defect found.

Read the command runner, remote and URL handling, failure_reason, hide_userinfo, path_too_long, is_trash_name and the trash sweeps. The long-path limit is checked before every command and the trash confirmation matches its callers; no provable defect found.

Read load/put/delete/nest/change/subtree and the terminal-sparing tests. A stored cycle could make subtree loop, but every writer goes through change under the store lock and nest refuses a group inside itself, so I could not build one; unproven, no finding.

Read land/land_inner, locate/project_of, the changed-file and clash checks, take_in_main, retry_behind and clear_after. The fast-forward versus merge choice and the behind retry match their callers; no provable defect found.

Read clean_url, repo_name, suggest_target, clone_into/clone_with, kill_tree and create_project. A pasted C:name value is not absolute, so the join nests it and create_dir fails rather than escaping a folder; no provable defect found.

Read parse_heads, fork_url, remote_for, push_target/push_args and scm_push_target with the GitHub tests. fork_url builds its owner/name tail from origin's own address, so the case-sensitive search cannot miss where I first suspected; no provable defect found.

Read the record readers and writers, project_for_path, the details form, places, forget/removal, the origin sweep and the icon cleaner. Six provable defects are listed here; the rest of the store and workspace flows I reviewed looked correct.

Read tidy_one/save_with/unfinished, the merge and clash paths, recover_at_start and the marker files. tidy_one refuses an unfinished merge but prepare_retire does not, which is F01; the rest of the quit and land merge flow matched its callers.

Read the whole file including its tests: glob, rules_of/ignored, main_of_linked, scan and the level order. rules_of rewriting the double-star prefix is F05; the rest of the walk, label and limit logic looked correct.
Read build_output, clear_workspace, after_land and is_link. Build output is cleared only from folders that are not links and only for paths the land touched; no provable defect found.
